subject: Re: NorthPeak + Redwood via AWS Marketplace — onboarding/entitlement questions
body:
From: Dana Whitaker <dwhitaker@northpeakanalytics.com>

Cc: Evan Cole <evan.cole@northpeakanalytics.com>, NorthPeak Security Team <security@northpeakanalytics.com>

Subject: NorthPeak + Redwood via AWS Marketplace — onboarding/entitlement questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for walking through the AWS Marketplace path on Friday.

Before we start the subscription internally, can you confirm a few details?

1) Entitlement timing: after we click “Subscribe” in AWS Marketplace, how long before Redwood recognizes the entitlement? Is it immediate or can there be delays?

2) Org linking: we already have a Redwood org created from a prior trial (not marketplace). Can we link the AWS subscription to that existing org, or do we have to create a new org?

3) Multiple subscriptions: our procurement team sometimes subscribes with one AWS account, while engineering runs workloads from another account. Does Redwood support linking multiple AWS Marketplace subscriptions to one org? What’s the recommended approach?

4) Support/SLA: what is the support channel + response time for Marketplace customers? Is it the same as your standard support, and do we need an enterprise support SKU/contract?

If you have a short doc we can send to procurement + security, that would help.

Best,
Dana Whitaker
Director, Data Platform
NorthPeak Analytics



From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: NorthPeak + Redwood via AWS Marketplace — onboarding/entitlement questions

Dana — sending answers inline below, and attaching our buyer-facing Marketplace FAQ draft (we’re using this for a few enterprise procurement cycles right now).

Attachment: Redwood_Marketplace_Onboarding_FAQ_draft_2026-02-07.pdf

1) Entitlement timing
- Typical: 5–15 minutes from AWS “Subscribe” to Redwood seeing the entitlement.
- Possible delay: it can take longer (we generally ask customers to allow up to ~60 minutes during peak partner-side propagation).
- If you hit an “entitlement not found” screen, the console provides a retry flow. If it’s still not showing after 60 minutes, we treat that as an onboarding issue and can escalate quickly (we’ve seen this occasionally when the subscribing AWS account differs from the account expected by the buyer).

2) Org linking (existing org)
- Yes — you can link the AWS Marketplace subscription to an existing Redwood org.
- The flow is: subscribe in AWS Marketplace → sign in to the Redwood Console → choose “Link subscription to an existing org” → select the org (or provide org ID) → complete verification.
- We recommend using the org that engineering will operate day-to-day (so usage, audit logs, API keys, etc. stay in one place).

3) Multiple subscriptions / multiple AWS accounts
- Two common patterns:
  a) One subscription per Redwood org (recommended): procurement subscribes once; the org is linked and all usage is metered to that entitlement.
  b) Multiple subscriptions linked to one org: supported in cases where procurement requires separate AWS payer/accounts. The key requirement is that each subscription is explicitly linked to the same Redwood org. This is useful if different business units must buy separately.
- If your procurement team subscribes under one AWS account and engineering operates under another, we can still make it work — the subscription/account used to subscribe matters for entitlement verification, but your application traffic does not need to originate from that same AWS account.

4) Support/SLA for Marketplace customers
- Hosted API via Marketplace includes Standard Support (email/ticket) by default.
- If you need a formal SLA / faster response times, that typically comes with Dedicated/Private + an enterprise support term (often transacted as part of a private offer).
- I’m looping in our Support escalation owner (Dev Patel) and our Enterprise onboarding stakeholder (Rachel Kim) to confirm the exact response-time language we should provide to your procurement/security teams.

Two clarifying questions so we give you the cleanest recommendation:
- Are you purchasing Hosted usage-based only, or is Dedicated capacity in scope this quarter?
- Do you expect procurement to require AWS Private Offer terms (vs public offer)?

Best,
Markus Klein
Solutions Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference

Adding support/SLA details that are safe to share in email (procurement-friendly wording):

Support channel (Marketplace customers)
- Primary: support@redwoodinference.com (email → ticket).
- For onboarding/entitlement issues specifically: include “Marketplace entitlement” in the subject line and we route it to the marketplace queue.

Response times
- Hosted (usage-based) Marketplace purchases include Standard Support:
  - Sev 1 (production down): target initial response within 1 business day.
  - Sev 2/3 (degraded/non-blocking/questions): target initial response within 2 business days.
  - Coverage: business hours (Mon–Fri) for the customer’s primary region.
- Dedicated/Private contracts commonly include an upgraded support term with faster response times and defined escalation paths. Those terms are documented in the order form / private offer and we can provide a redlined support exhibit if needed.

Escalation path for entitlement/provisioning delays
- If entitlement linking is delayed >60 minutes after subscription, we treat it as an onboarding incident and escalate to engineering. (This is the same path we used on SUP-4821 recently.)

Rachel may want to add anything around enterprise onboarding expectations, but the above is the standard language we’ve been using.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Support Escalation Owner
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: NorthPeak + Redwood via AWS Marketplace — onboarding/entitlement questions

Dana — closing the loop with the support/SLA language from Dev (below), plus one recommendation based on what you described.

Recommendation for your org/account setup
- If procurement will subscribe using a central AWS payer account, that’s totally fine.
- Engineering does NOT need to run workloads from that same AWS account. The important part is: whoever completes the “link subscription → Redwood org” step uses the correct subscription context when verifying.
- Given you already have a Redwood trial org, we should link the Marketplace subscription to that existing org to avoid splitting keys/usage/audit logs.

Support/SLA (Marketplace)
- Hosted Marketplace includes Standard Support via support@redwoodinference.com.
- If you need faster response times / formal SLA language, that’s typically packaged with Dedicated/Private + enterprise support terms (often through an AWS Private Offer).

Next steps (if helpful)
1) You subscribe in AWS Marketplace.
2) Reply to this thread with a timestamp + the subscribing AWS account ID (or just the last 4) so we can sanity-check entitlement propagation if needed.
3) We schedule a 20-min “first-call” working session to ensure your org is linked and you get to first successful request.

Let me know whether Dedicated capacity is in-scope for Q1/Q2; if yes, I’ll pull in the right folks to align on the correct Marketplace SKU/private offer structure.

Best,
Markus
